facts.statement: The genus Millerosteus was described by Stensiö in 1959.
Millerosteus lived during the Early Givetian stage of the Middle Devonian period.
Fossils of Millerosteus date from 393.47 to 382.31 million years ago, spanning the Eifelian to Givetian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Eifelian to Givetian (393.47 to 382.31 million years ago)

facts.statement: Fossils of Millerosteus have been found in Orkney and Caithness, Scotland.
facts.quote: Fossils are found in Orkney and Caithness, Scotland.

facts.statement: Millerosteus was a small placoderm reaching a body length of 14 cm.
facts.quote: It was a small placoderm with a body length of 14 cm.

facts.statement: Millerosteus is one of the few arthrodire genera known from specimens preserving the entire skeleton.
facts.quote: Millerosteus is one of the few arthrodires known from specimens preserving the entire skeleton.

facts.statement: Millerosteus is classified as an extinct genus of coccosteid arthrodire placoderm.
facts.quote: Millerosteus is an extinct genus of coccosteid arthrodire placoderm from the Early Givetian stage of the Middle Devonian period.

facts.statement: Millerosteus belongs to the family Coccosteidae, the clade Coccosteomorphi, and the superclade Eubrachythoraci.
facts.quote: Millerosteus is a member of the family Coccosteidae, which belongs to the clade Coccosteomorphi, one of the two major clades within Eubrachythoraci.

facts.statement: Millerosteus is classified within the class Placodermi.
